question.leadin: This leader and his mistress Claretta Petacci were allegedly hung on meathooks.
question.text: Name this former Socialist and fascist world leader. He was nicknamed "Il Duce" (eel doo-chay) and was supported by the paramilitary Blackshirts.
question.clue: This leader used claims of native irredentism to force King Zog into exile and justify his country's occupation of Albania.

swap.leadin: Name the following Italian cities that were powerful during the Middle Ages and Renaissance.
swap.text: Under the Doge Enrico Dandolo, this city provided support for troops during the Fourth Crusade.
swap.clue: This city-state's hinterland, the "Domini di Terraferma," was partitioned between Austria and the Cisalpine Republic by the provisions of the 1797 Treaty of Campo Formio.

question.leadin: Name these Italian cities important to Renaissance politics.
question.text: This Lombard city and former seat of the Visconti was once reconquered from France by Ludovico Sforza, known as "Il Moro;" it eventually passed to the Habsburgs.
question.clue: During the Middle Ages, this city was repeatedly razed to the ground Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, after taking charge of the rebel Lombard league.

swap.leadin: Give the following about colorful symbols throughout history.
swap.text: The Redshirts were loyal supporters of this Italian unifier who led the Expedition of a Thousand and fought in the Uruguayan Civil War.
swap.clue: He was once offered command on the Union side of the Civil War, and one campaign by this man began at Marsala.

question.text: This secret society advocated Italian unification after the Napoleonic invasion, opposing Napoleon's stooge Murat, and attempted several revolts, including one in Naples against the Bourbons.
question.clue: Their assemblies occurred in houses called "baraccas," and representatives from several Vendite met at the Alta Vendita.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about powerful Italian families during the Renaissance.
swap.text: The excesses of the Italian Borgia family were targeted by this Dominican Friar who organized the 1497 Bonfire of the Vanities.
swap.clue: His Compendium of Revelations contains his dichotomy of prophecies and images of a black cross above Rome and a gold cross above Jerusalem.

question.leadin: This battle was preceded by eleven earlier battles, all near the same northern Italian river.
question.text: Name this battle, also known as the Twelfth Battle of the Isonzo. Luigi Cadorna was replaced as chief of staff after this disastrous defeat for the Italians.
question.answerHtml: Battle of Caporetto (accept Battle of Kobarid; accept Battle of Karfreit)
question.clue: Luigi Cadorna was dismissed after this battle, during which Erwin Rommel earned the Pour le Merite for capturing 9,000 men.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about historical flags featuring disembodied heads.
swap.text: Four disembodied moor's heads are featured on the flag of this island which was unified with the northern Italian region of Piedmont in an early kingdom. Victor Emmanuel II was a king of this Mediterranean island before becoming king of Italy.
swap.clue: The House of Savoy ruled this island in an alliance with Piedmont until Victor Emmanuel II, its king, completed the Risorgimento.

question.text: Manius Valerius Maximus brought the first Roman sundial back from the city of Catania in this region. This region, a major source of grain for the Roman Republic, was the site of the first two Servile Wars.
question.clue: A disastrous military campaign in this region was supported by Alcibiades and contributed to Athens's defeat in the Peloponnesian War.

swap.leadin: The monarch of the losing side in this battle was taken to Spain and forced to sign the Treaty of Madrid in its aftermath.
swap.text: Identify this 1525 victory for Charles V over Francis I in the Italian Wars.
swap.clue: The final active Yorkist pretender to the English throne, Richard de la Pole, was killed at this battle.

question.leadin: A member of this family married Alfonso I d'Este ("di-ES-tay") and supposedly used a hollow ring to poison her enemies.
question.text: Name this family of the noblewoman Lucrezia. Cesare ("tsay-ZAR-ay"), another member of this family, is often cited as an example in Machiavelli's The Prince.
question.clue: Popes from this family included Calixtus III and Alexander VI.

swap.leadin: Name these inventors of the early 20th and late 19th century.
swap.text: This Italian physicist, who won the 1909 Nobel Prize, extended the work of Heinrich Hertz and was one of the first people to transmit radio waves. He is known as the inventor of the radio.
swap.clue: This man's first transmission was, "Are you ready," and at Toynbee Hall, he gave the lecture, "Telegraphy without Wires."

question.leadin: Name these influential works of pre-modern Italy.
question.text: This monumental epic poem has Dante journey through the Inferno, Purgatory, and Paradise.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the rise of a Frankish king with an unfortunate epithet, Pepin the Short.
swap.text: Pope Zachary condoned Pepin's coup to gain Frankish support against these people whose leader Desiderius was later crushed by Charlemagne. These people named a League that defeated Frederick Barbarossa at Legnano ("len-YAH-noh").
swap.answerHtml: Lombards [or Longobards or Longobardi; accept Lombardy or Lombardia; accept Lombard League or Lega Lombarda]
swap.clue: The death of that king, Liutprand, is the final event in a history of these peoples written by Paul the Deacon.

question.leadin: Conspiracy theorists have accused this organization of masterminding the death of "God's Banker," Roberto Calvi.
question.text: Name this secretive crypto-fascist masonic lodge that operated in Italy until 1981, when police found its charter and membership list while searching its leader's mansion.
question.clue: The discovery of this "shadow government" led to Prime Minister Arnaldo Forlani resigning.

swap.text: Constant wars over this peninsula against the Habsburgs, often involving condottieri mercenaries, prompted France to ally with the Ottoman Empire.
swap.clue: Legend states females on this peninsula gave themselves to invaders to stop a war, an act known as the Rape of the Sabine Women.

question.leadin: Following the death of Pope Paul I, this man supported the candidacy of Antipope Philip.
question.text: Identify this last king of the Lombards who was defeated by an ally of Pope Adrian I.
question.clue: This leader's people were profiled by his rival's courtier, Paul the Deacon, who sought the hand of this man's daughter for his Lord.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Italy in the 1970s.
swap.text: In the late 1970s, Enrico Berlinguer's ("bare-leen-GWER's") Italian Communist Party and Aldo Moro's Christian Democracy unexpectedly formed a coalitionary alliance known by this two-word term.
swap.answerHtml: “historic compromise” [or “compromesso storico”; accept Third Phrase or Terza Fase; accept Democratic Alternative or Alternativa Democratica]
swap.clue: This unexpected alliance between the PCI and Christian Democracy.

question.leadin: This body was established following the conspiracy of Baiamonte Tiepolo. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this Italian political organization founded by Piero Gradenigo in 1310. Elected from members of the Great Council, it officially held power over matters of peace, coinage and sodomy.
question.clue: After the Bajamonte Tiepolo against the Doge in 1310, this secretive council was created, named for the original number of its members, and given emergency powers in Venice. It was led by men called Capi who were confined to live in the Doge's Palace.

swap.leadin: King Charles Robert I of this dynasty appears on the 200 Forint bill in Hungary, which he ruled from 1312 to 1342.
swap.text: Name this royal house from the namesake area of France, who descend from a younger son of Blanche of Castile and more notably ruled Sicily and Naples.
swap.clue: In 1460, Skanderbeg led an expedition to help Ferdinand I of Naples defend against this house. A member of this house, Charles II, defended against the House of Barcelona in the War of the Sicilian Vespers.
